stage1.impression: Clean, symmetrical living-room set with two milk-carton speakers flanking a turntable; the product reads instantly and the red/white identity is strong. But the lighting is flat and frontal: the white bodies sit near one value with a bright lift toward their bases that reads as self-glow, the speakers sit on the sideboard without convincing contact shadows, and a third of the frame is empty beige wall.

blocking_9: The sideboard must read as veneered furniture: grain and figure on the doors (middle-door lum_range 12-32), not a flat tan slab whose only texture is a 6.4 px vertical ribbing of +/-1.9 levels (lum_range 8.7 now).
The drivers must read as hi-fi drivers: woofer-cone median 21-30 with lower cone, upper cone and dust cap separated (now 14.2; upper cone 7-8, cap 17).
Both roofs must hold #C62828: no front-slope patch beyond dE 6 (right roof above-left of the insert is (213, 85, 87), dE 11.3; the left roof's matching patch is dE 7.5).

The lacquer fronts' window reflections must grade instead of plateauing: both strips print a flat band about 60 px wide over their full 160 px height (228-231 left, 224-228 right), above the 226 knee, so they read as glow rather than a reflected window.

The room must read lived-in: at least one organic or personal accent besides the turntable and the single print, placed without crowding the pair (the sideboard top has only 0.14-0.16 m free beside the turntable, and the band above the speakers is bare wall).
The pair must carry the frame: the speakers fill 58% of the frame height under a 285 px (32%) band of bare wall; a 9 holds them nearer 65-70% so the waveguides and drivers read at homepage size.

changes.problem: The sideboard, the bottom fifth of the frame and the furniture carrying the pair, reads as a tan cardboard slab: its doors are one flat value whose only texture is a regular vertical ribbing, with no wood figure, which undercuts the premium read.

evidence.measured: middle door lum_median 135.2, lum_range 8.7 (p5 132.0, p95 140.7); rows 850-890 trace a strictly periodic ribbing, period 6.4 px, +/-1.9 levels (peak-to-peak 3.8), and no other figure; left door [0, 830, 360, 897] lum_range 6.3; front band [0, 820, 1350, 900] rgb (149, 133, 113).

changes.expected: Doors and top take a sliced veneer under satin lacquer, grain along the piece with a book-matched figure per door; middle-door lum_range rises from 8.7 to about 16-26 while its median stays within 128-146 (the band c3 set), the 6.4 px ribbing disappears and the top reads as lacquered wood; nothing on the speakers changes.

changes.problem: The woofers read as black holes: the paper cones sit at a median of 14 with their upper half at 7-8, so the cone's flare, the dust cap and the surround roll, the details that say hi-fi, barely separate.

evidence.measured: vertical trace through the right woofer: trim ring 82, surround 48 then 30, upper cone 7.2-7.6, dust cap 17, lower cone 17-20, lower surround 34-41, ring 57; part:woofer-cone lum_median 14.2, p5 6.9, p95 24.0; the cone mirrors lamp key over ceiling 28%, rug 20%, floor 12%.

changes.expected: A soft strip about 31 degrees above the woofer axis, linked to the drivers alone: the lower cone rises to about 30-40 while the upper cone stays near 10-14, so the flare reads as a gradient; the dust cap takes a highlight on its upper half (about 30); the surround's top roll prints 60-90; cone median about 25, p95 about 40; the white baffle, trim ring, plinth and wall do not change.

changes.problem: The roofs' front slopes go coral where they mirror the brightest part of the roof_sheen ramp: the closer right speaker's slope lifts to (213, 85, 87) above-left of the waveguide, so the brand red reads salmon on the roof beside a deeper fin and plinth.

evidence.measured: rgb (213, 85, 87), lum 112.1, dE2000 11.3 vs #C62828; mirrors panel roof_sheen 100%; down the slope the sheen falls 120 to 85; right of the insert [1136, 325, 1157, 372] dE 4.6; the left roof's matching patch [177, 316, 190, 336] (203, 70, 74) dE 7.5; the fin [990, 289, 1160, 306] (184, 29, 20) dE 4.7.

changes.expected: The sheen keeps its ramp from the fin down at about half the lift: the right slope's patch comes to about (204, 62, 64), dE 4-5.5, and the left roof's to about dE 3-4; both slopes still lighten 15-25 levels toward the fin so the lacquer reads, and the gable-block's lit face stays within dE 1.

out_of_scope.request: A lighter grey or textured cone on the woofers so the drivers show detail without extra light
out_of_scope.why: The SB17NRX2C35-8's black paper cone is the product's own material and is fixed; at median 14 it is the darkest product part, so light linked to the drivers (c2) is the only lever.

out_of_scope.request: Print the Nutrition Facts on each speaker's outer side, mirrored, so the right speaker's panel faces the camera
out_of_scope.why: The panel's place and layout are fixed marks; from this camera the right speaker shows its panel edge-on, 27 px wide and illegible, against 55 px on the left, so the pair reads less like a mirrored set.
